column1: 25:1|Of David.\nTo you, LORD, I lift up my life.|Keep title and lifted life as an act of trust.
25:2|My God, I trust in you.\nDo not let me be put to shame;\ndo not let my enemies celebrate my downfall.|Clarify the object of enemy triumph without erasing shame.
25:3|Indeed, no one who waits for you will be put to shame.\nLet shame fall on those who betray others without cause.|Preserve the contrast between waiting and groundless treachery.
25:4|Show me your ways, LORD;\nteach me your paths.|Retain paired journey images and direct appeal.
25:5|Lead me in your truth and teach me,\nfor you are the God who saves me.\nI wait for you all day long.|Connect guidance with rescue and sustained waiting.
25:6|Remember your compassion, LORD, and your faithful love;\nthey have been yours from long ago.|Keep divine remembering and the antiquity of mercy.

25:7|Do not remember my youthful sins or my rebellions.\nRemember me according to your faithful love,\nfor the sake of your goodness, LORD.|Retain the threefold remembering contrast and acknowledged rebellion.
25:8|The LORD is good and upright;\nthat is why he teaches sinners the way.|Make the causal link audible while retaining sinners as learners.
25:9|He leads the humble in what is just\nand teaches the humble his way.|Preserve humble repeated and justice linked to guidance.
25:10|All the LORD’s paths are faithful love and truth\nfor those who keep his covenant and his testimonies.|Keep covenant and the relational qualification.
25:11|For your name’s sake, LORD,\nforgive my wrongdoing, great as it is.|Preserve the greatness of guilt as part of the appeal.
25:12|Who is the person who reveres the LORD?\nThe LORD will teach that person the way to choose.|Clarify the teacher while leaving the choice’s agency open in a note.
25:13|That person will rest in well-being,\nand their offspring will inherit the land.|Retain both present well-being and generational land promise.
25:14|The LORD shares his counsel with those who revere him;\nhe makes his covenant known to them.|Render confidential council access naturally without reducing it to information.
25:15|My eyes are always turned toward the LORD,\nfor he will free my feet from the net.|Keep eyes and trapped feet in their paired image.
25:16|Turn toward me and be gracious to me,\nfor I am alone and afflicted.|Preserve the speaker’s loneliness alongside affliction.
25:17|My heart’s troubles have grown wide;\nbring me out of my distress.|Keep the ironic widening of trouble and release from constriction.
25:18|Look at my affliction and hardship,\nand forgive all my sins.|Retain suffering and sin together without declaring one caused the other.
25:19|Look how many my enemies are,\nhow violently they hate me.|Keep the repeated look and violent hatred.
25:20|Guard my life and rescue me.\nDo not let me be put to shame,\nfor I have taken refuge in you.|Connect refuge with the appeal for life and honor.
25:21|May integrity and uprightness guard me,\nfor I wait for you.|Retain personified virtues and the waiting refrain.
25:22|God, redeem Israel\nfrom all its troubles.|Preserve the final widening from individual to Israel.
26:1|Of David.\nVindicate me, LORD, for I have walked with integrity.\nI have trusted in the LORD without wavering.|Keep the title and integrity claim without claiming absolute sinlessness.
26:2|Examine me, LORD, and test me;\nrefine my kidneys and my heart.|Follow the read imperative and preserve the ancient bodily image.
26:3|Your faithful love is before my eyes,\nand I walk in your truth.|Keep seeing and walking as sustained orientation.
26:4|I do not sit with deceitful people\nor go along with those who hide what they are.|Render concealed identity without inventing a named sect.
26:5|I hate the gathering of evildoers\nand will not sit with the wicked.|Retain the speaker’s hatred and refusal of company.
26:6|I wash my hands in innocence\nand walk around your altar, LORD,|Preserve ritual and ethical imagery and continue into purpose.
26:7|to raise a voice of thanksgiving\nand recount all your wonders.|Keep the audible praise and full scope of wonders.
26:8|LORD, I love the house where you dwell,\nthe place where your glory makes its home.|Retain the repeated dwelling language.
26:9|Do not sweep my life away with sinners,\nmy life with men who shed blood,|Make gathering in death readable and preserve bloodshed.
26:10|whose hands are full of schemes\nand whose right hands overflow with bribes.|Retain hands and specific corruption.
26:11|But I will walk with integrity.\nRedeem me and be gracious to me.|Keep integrity alongside need for grace.
26:12|My feet stand on level ground;\nin the assemblies I will bless the LORD.|Conclude with secure footing and public praise.
27:1|Of David.\nThe LORD is my light and my salvation—whom should I fear?\nThe LORD is my life’s stronghold—whom should I dread?|Keep the paired confidence questions and protective images.
27:2|When evildoers came at me to devour my flesh,\nmy adversaries and enemies stumbled and fell.|Preserve predatory violence and the enemies’ reversal.
27:3|Though an army camps against me, my heart will not fear.\nThough war rises against me, even then I will trust.|Retain escalating threats and inward confidence.

27:4|One thing I have asked of the LORD; this is what I seek:\nto dwell in the LORD’s house all my life,\nto gaze on the LORD’s beauty and seek him in his temple.|Preserve singular desire and the uncertain seeking verb without reducing it to attendance.
27:5|On a day of trouble he will hide me in his shelter,\nconceal me in the cover of his tent,\nand lift me high onto a rock.|Retain three protective actions and concrete places.
27:6|Now my head will rise above the enemies around me.\nIn his tent I will offer sacrifices with shouts of joy;\nI will sing and make music to the LORD.|Keep raised head and sacrificial celebration.
27:7|Hear my voice when I call, LORD;\nbe gracious to me and answer.|Let confidence turn to petition without smoothing the shift.
27:8|My heart speaks for you: “Seek my face.”\nYour face, LORD, I will seek.|Preserve difficult shifts of speaker and person with a note.

27:9|Do not hide your face from me
or turn your servant away in anger.
You have been my help.
Do not abandon or forsake me, God who saves me.|Keep repeated abandonment appeals and remembered help.
27:10|Though my father and mother forsake me,\nthe LORD will take me in.|Retain the extremity of parental loss and divine welcome.
27:11|Teach me your way, LORD;\nlead me on a level path because of those watching for my fall.|Clarify hostile watchers while keeping the path image.
27:12|Do not hand me over to my adversaries’ desires.\nFalse witnesses have risen against me, breathing violence.|Keep judicial threat and the breath image.
27:13|If I had not trusted that I would see the LORD’s goodness\nin the land of the living—|Preserve the marked Hebrew conditional and unfinished sentence.
27:14|Wait for the LORD.\nBe strong, and let your heart take courage.\nWait for the LORD.|Retain the repeated summons and inward courage.

28:1|Of David.
To you I call, LORD, my rock.
Do not be deaf to me.
If you stay silent, I will be like those who descend to the pit.|Keep hearing/silence contrast and the threat of death.
28:2|Hear my plea for mercy when I cry to you,\nwhen I lift my hands toward your holy inner sanctuary.|Clarify the temple location while preserving raised hands.
28:3|Do not drag me away with the wicked, with evildoers,\nwho speak peace to their neighbors while harboring evil.|Retain deceptive peace and the request for distinct treatment.

28:4|Give them what their deeds deserve,
what their evil actions deserve.
Repay the work of their hands;
return to them what they have earned.|Keep the insistent repetitions of retribution.
28:5|They pay no attention to the LORD’s deeds,\nto the work of his hands.\nHe will tear them down and never build them up.|Retain the human/divine hands contrast and building metaphor.
28:6|Blessed be the LORD!\nHe has heard my plea for mercy.|Keep the turn to answered prayer.
28:7|The LORD is my strength and my shield.\nMy heart trusted him, and I was helped.\nMy heart leaps for joy; with my song I thank him.|Preserve trust, help, and rejoicing in connected sequence.
28:8|The LORD is their strength,\na stronghold of salvation for his anointed.|Retain pinned their rather than silently replacing it with his people.
28:9|Save your people and bless your inheritance.\nShepherd them and carry them forever.|Keep collective inheritance and the caring shepherd actions.
29:1|A psalm of David.\nGive the LORD his due, you sons of gods;\ngive the LORD glory and strength.|Preserve heavenly assembly language with explanatory vocabulary.
29:2|Give the LORD the glory of his name;\nbow before the LORD in holy splendor.|Keep liturgical repetition and ambiguous holy adornment.
29:3|The LORD’s voice is over the waters;\nthe God of glory thunders,\nthe LORD over mighty waters.|Preserve voice/thunder parallelism and repeated waters.
29:4|The LORD’s voice is powerful;\nthe LORD’s voice is majestic.|Retain the central repeated subject.
29:5|The LORD’s voice breaks cedars;\nthe LORD shatters the cedars of Lebanon.|Keep specific trees and region with intensified action.
29:6|He makes Lebanon skip like a calf,\nSirion like a young wild ox.|Keep mountains personified as leaping animals.
29:7|The LORD’s voice cuts out flames of fire.|Preserve the striking lightning-like image without replacing it with an explanation.
29:8|The LORD’s voice makes the wilderness writhe;\nthe LORD makes the wilderness of Kadesh writhe.|Retain repeated action and named wilderness.
29:9|The LORD’s voice brings deer into labor\nand strips the forests bare.\nIn his temple everything cries, “Glory!”|Follow pointed deer reading and retain the cosmic acclamation.
29:10|The LORD sat enthroned over the flood;\nthe LORD sits as king forever.|Keep the flood term and past-to-enduring kingship.
29:11|May the LORD give strength to his people;\nmay the LORD bless his people with peace.|Read the concluding imperfects as blessing while retaining strength and peace.

30:1|A psalm. A song for the dedication of the house. Of David.\nI will lift you high, LORD, for you drew me up\nand did not let my enemies rejoice over me.|Include the entire title and the lifting wordplay.
30:2|LORD my God, I cried to you,\nand you healed me.|Keep the direct sequence of appeal and healing.
30:3|LORD, you brought my life up from Sheol;\nyou kept me alive, saving me from going down to the pit.|Follow read my going down and retain Sheol alongside pit.
30:4|Sing praise to the LORD, you faithful ones;\ngive thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.|Preserve the communal summons and holy remembrance expression.
30:5|His anger lasts a moment; his favor brings a lifetime.\nWeeping may stay for the night,\nbut a cry of joy comes with morning.|Keep duration contrast and weeping as an overnight guest.
30:6|When I was secure, I said,\n“I will never be shaken.”|Mark remembered confidence as the speaker’s earlier claim.
30:7|LORD, in your favor you made my mountain stand strong.\nYou hid your face, and I was terrified.|Preserve the difficult mountain image and sudden vulnerability.
30:8|To you, LORD, I called;\nto the Lord I pleaded:|Distinguish divine name and Adonai title.
30:9|“What gain is there in my blood, in my going down to the pit?\nWill the dust thank you? Will it tell of your faithfulness?|Retain the appeal against death and the voice of dust.
30:10|Hear, LORD, and be gracious to me.\nLORD, be my help!”|Keep repeated address and close the plea.
30:11|You turned my mourning into dancing;\nyou loosened my sackcloth and clothed me with joy,|Preserve the changing garments and embodied reversal.
30:12|so my glory may sing to you and not be silent.\nLORD my God, I will thank you forever.|Keep pinned glory with a note and the purpose of renewed life.

31:1|For the music leader. A psalm of David.\nIn you, LORD, I take refuge; never let me be put to shame.\nRescue me in your righteousness.|Bind title and opening appeal; retain righteousness as ground of rescue.
31:2|Bend your ear toward me; hurry to rescue me.\nBe my rock of refuge, a fortress to save me.|Keep bodily listening and defensive images.
31:3|You are my crag and my fortress.\nFor your name’s sake, lead me and guide me.|Retain remembered protection as reason for guidance.
31:4|Free me from the net they hid for me,\nfor you are my stronghold.|Keep concealed danger and direct trust.
31:5|Into your hand I entrust my spirit.\nYou have redeemed me, LORD, faithful God.|Preserve entrusted spirit without importing a later narrative setting.
31:6|I hate those who cling to empty idols;\nmy trust is in the LORD.|Retain pinned first-person hatred and contrast of allegiances.
31:7|I will rejoice and be glad in your faithful love.\nYou have seen my affliction; you know my life’s distress.|Keep seeing and knowing as attentive divine response.
31:8|You have not shut me into the enemy’s hand;\nyou have set my feet in a broad place.|Preserve confinement and spacious freedom.
31:9|Be gracious to me, LORD, for I am in distress.\nMy eyes waste away with grief, my whole being and my body too.|Retain embodied exhaustion across the whole person.
31:10|My life drains away in sorrow, my years in sighing.\nMy strength fails because of my wrongdoing; my bones waste away.|Keep pinned guilt rather than substituting affliction.

31:11|Because of all my foes I have become an object of scorn,\nespecially to my neighbors, a terror to my acquaintances.\nThose who see me outside flee from me.|Preserve the widening social rejection.
31:12|I have slipped from memory like someone dead;\nI am like a broken vessel.|Keep forgotten death and discarded-object imagery.
31:13|I hear the whispering of many—terror on every side!\nThey gather against me and plot to take my life.|Retain fear refrain and lethal conspiracy.
31:14|But I trust in you, LORD.\nI say, “You are my God.”|Keep the explicit turn toward trust.
31:15|My times are in your hand.\nRescue me from the hand of my enemies and pursuers.|Retain contrasted hands and the open meaning of times.
31:16|Let your face shine on your servant;\nsave me in your faithful love.|Preserve the blessing image in a personal plea.
31:17|LORD, do not let me be put to shame, for I call on you.\nLet the wicked be ashamed and fall silent in Sheol.|Keep the severe reversal and realm of death.
31:18|Silence lying lips\nthat speak insolently against the righteous with pride and contempt.|Retain the nature and target of hostile speech.
31:19|How abundant is the goodness you have stored up for those who revere you,\nwhich you show to those who take refuge in you, before all people!|Keep stored goodness becoming publicly visible.
31:20|You hide them in the shelter of your presence from human plots;\nyou keep them safe in a shelter from quarreling tongues.|Preserve shelter repeated and speech as a threat.
31:21|Blessed be the LORD!\nHe showed me wondrous faithful love in a besieged city.|Choose besieged rather than fortified and note the ambiguity.
31:22|In my panic I said, “I am cut off from your sight!”\nYet you heard my plea when I cried to you for help.|Retain the contrast between fearful perception and being heard.
31:23|Love the LORD, all you faithful ones.\nThe LORD guards the faithful and repays the proud in full.|Keep communal appeal and asymmetric outcomes.
31:24|Be strong, and let your hearts take courage,\nall you who hope in the LORD.|Preserve the shared closing exhortation.
32:1|Of David. A maskil.\nHappy is the one whose rebellion is forgiven, whose sin is covered.|Retain title and two images of forgiveness.
32:2|Happy is the person whose wrongdoing the LORD does not count against them,\nin whose spirit there is no deceit.|Clarify accounting idiom while preserving inner honesty.
32:3|When I kept silent, my bones wore out\nthrough my groaning all day long.|Retain the paradox of silence and anguished noise.
32:4|Day and night your hand weighed on me;\nmy vitality dried up in summer’s heat. Selah.|Keep heavy hand and drying life imagery.

32:5|I made my sin known to you; I did not cover my wrongdoing.\nI said, “I will confess my rebellions to the LORD,”\nand you forgave the guilt of my sin. Selah.|Preserve cover/uncover contrast and confession followed by forgiveness.
32:6|So let everyone faithful pray to you while you may be found.\nWhen mighty waters flood, they will not reach that person.|Supply found object cautiously and retain flood protection.
32:7|You are my hiding place. You guard me from distress;\nyou surround me with songs of deliverance. Selah.|Keep surrounding songs and protective refuge.
32:8|I will give you insight and teach you the way to go;\nI will counsel you with my eye upon you.|Leave the unmarked speaker open and preserve watchful counsel.
32:9|Do not be like a horse or mule without understanding,\nheld in check by bit and bridle,\nor it will not come near you.|Retain animal restraint and difficult final relation.
32:10|The wicked have many sorrows,\nbut faithful love surrounds the one who trusts the LORD.|Keep the contrast and surrounding motif.
32:11|Rejoice in the LORD and be glad, you righteous;\nshout for joy, all you upright in heart.|Retain both groups in the communal invitation.
33:1|Shout for joy in the LORD, you righteous!\nPraise is fitting for the upright.|Preserve the call and its stated suitability.
33:2|Thank the LORD with the lyre;\nmake music to him on a ten-stringed harp.|Keep instrument distinction and number.
33:3|Sing him a new song;\nplay skillfully, with shouts of joy.|Retain newness and skilled audible celebration.
33:4|The LORD’s word is upright;\nall his work is done faithfully.|Keep word and work in parallel.
33:5|He loves righteousness and justice;\nthe earth is full of the LORD’s faithful love.|Retain the three linked moral and relational terms.
33:6|By the LORD’s word the heavens were made,\nand all their host by the breath of his mouth.|Keep speech and breath as creation imagery.
33:7|He gathers the sea’s waters into a heap;\nhe places the deeps in storehouses.|Preserve pinned heap and ancient spatial images.
33:8|Let all the earth fear the LORD;\nlet everyone in the world stand in awe of him.|Keep universal scope and paired reverent responses.
33:9|He spoke, and it came to be;\nhe commanded, and it stood firm.|Retain concise divine speech and resulting existence.
33:10|The LORD frustrates the nations’ counsel\nand thwarts the peoples’ plans.|Preserve counsel/plans as repeated terms for later contrast.
33:11|The LORD’s counsel stands forever,\nthe plans of his heart through every generation.|Retain the contrast of enduring divine purpose.
33:12|Happy is the nation whose God is the LORD,\nthe people he chose as his own inheritance.|Keep election and inheritance without substituting a modern nation.
33:13|The LORD looks down from heaven\nand sees all humanity.|Preserve the comprehensive divine gaze.
33:14|From his dwelling place he watches\neveryone who lives on earth—|Continue the same gaze across the verse boundary.
33:15|he who forms all their hearts\nand understands everything they do.|Keep shared formation and individual actions.
33:16|A king is not saved by a great army;\na warrior does not escape by great strength.|Retain the two human power claims denied.
33:17|A horse is a false hope for victory;\nits great power cannot bring escape.|Keep military horse and insufficiency of strength.
33:18|Look, the LORD’s eye is on those who revere him,\non those who hope in his faithful love,|Retain the eye image and waiting recipients.
33:19|to rescue their lives from death\nand keep them alive in famine.|Preserve two concrete threats to life.
33:20|We wait for the LORD;\nhe is our help and our shield.|Mark the shift into shared first-person trust.
33:21|Our hearts rejoice in him,\nfor we trust in his holy name.|Connect rejoicing with trust without removing name language.
33:22|Let your faithful love rest on us, LORD,\nas we place our hope in you.|Keep the responsive relation of hope and petition.

34:1|Of David, when he changed his behavior before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he left.\nI will bless the LORD at all times; his praise will always be in my mouth.|Retain the title’s Abimelech without harmonizing to Achish.
34:2|I will boast in the LORD;\nlet the humble hear and be glad.|Keep personal testimony inviting humble hearers.
34:3|Magnify the LORD with me;\nlet us lift his name high together.|Retain corporate praise and raised name.
34:4|I sought the LORD, and he answered me;\nhe rescued me from everything I feared.|Preserve seeking, answer, and comprehensive rescue.
34:5|Those who look to him shine with joy;\ntheir faces need never be ashamed.|Express radiance without losing face/shame imagery.
34:6|This afflicted person cried out, and the LORD heard;\nhe saved him from all his troubles.|Keep the speaker’s demonstrative testimony and singular sufferer.
34:7|The LORD’s messenger camps around those who revere him\nand rescues them.|Retain encampment and messenger without a later identification.
34:8|Taste and see that the LORD is good.\nHappy is the one who takes refuge in him.|Retain the memorable sensory invitation.
34:9|Revere the LORD, you his holy ones;\nthose who revere him lack nothing.|Keep repeated reverence and broad wisdom claim.
34:10|Young lions go hungry and lack food,\nbut those who seek the LORD will lack no good thing.|Retain animal contrast and the poem’s unqualified promise.
34:11|Come, children, listen to me;\nI will teach you reverence for the LORD.|Preserve the teacher’s familial address.
34:12|Who desires life\nand loves to see good days?|Keep the rhetorical invitation before instruction.
34:13|Guard your tongue from evil\nand your lips from deceitful speech.|Retain paired speech organs and responsibility.
34:14|Turn from evil and do good;\nseek peace and pursue it.|Preserve active pursuit and balanced commands.
34:15|The LORD’s eyes are toward the righteous,\nhis ears toward their cry for help.|Keep attentive bodily imagery.
34:16|The LORD’s face is against evildoers,\nto erase their memory from the earth.|Retain severe face and memory judgment.
34:17|They cry out, and the LORD hears;\nhe rescues them from all their troubles.|Leave the resumed righteous referent as a pronoun with context intact.
34:18|The LORD is near to the brokenhearted\nand saves those whose spirits are crushed.|Keep nearness and rescue as distinct responses.
34:19|The righteous face many troubles,\nbut the LORD rescues them from them all.|Preserve suffering alongside deliverance claim.
34:20|He guards all their bones;\nnot one of them is broken.|Retain bodily preservation without importing later fulfillment language.
34:21|Evil will kill the wicked;\nthose who hate the righteous will be held guilty.|Keep evil as destructive agent and legal consequence.
34:22|The LORD redeems the lives of his servants;\nnone who take refuge in him will be held guilty.|Repeat legal outcome in contrasting conclusion.
35:1|Of David.\nContend, LORD, with those who contend with me;\nfight those who fight me.|Preserve matching legal and military appeals.
35:2|Take up shield and great shield;\nrise to help me.|Retain two defensive implements.
35:3|Draw your spear and block the way of my pursuers.\nSay to me, “I am your salvation.”|Choose block as verb and make the reassurance audible.
35:4|Let those seeking my life be ashamed and disgraced;\nlet those plotting my harm retreat in humiliation.|Retain parallel wishes against attackers.
35:5|Let them be chaff before the wind,\nwith the LORD’s messenger driving them away.|Keep the windblown chaff and divine messenger.
35:6|Let their path be dark and slippery,\nwith the LORD’s messenger pursuing them.|Retain pursuit and dangerous path imagery.
35:7|Without cause they hid their net in a pit for me;\nwithout cause they dug a trap for my life.|Retain twice-repeated causelessness and compressed trap image.
35:8|Let ruin catch the enemy unaware;\nlet the net he hid catch him;\nlet him fall into it, into ruin.|Make the singular enemy clear while preserving self-entrapment.
35:9|Then I will rejoice in the LORD,\ndelighting in his salvation.|Keep personal response to deliverance.

35:10|All my bones will say, “LORD, who is like you?\nYou rescue the afflicted from those too strong for them,\nthe afflicted and needy from the one who robs them.”|Retain speaking bones and protection of vulnerable people.
35:11|Violent witnesses rise up;\nthey question me about things I know nothing of.|Keep legal violence and unsupported accusations.
35:12|They repay my good with evil,\nleaving my life bereaved.|Preserve bereavement metaphor rather than generic sadness.
35:13|Yet when they were ill, I wore sackcloth\nand humbled myself with fasting;\nmy prayer returned to my bosom.|Retain difficult returning-prayer image for the note.
35:14|I went about as though grieving for a friend or brother;\nbowed in mourning, as for my mother.|Keep intimate relationships and embodied mourning.
35:15|But when I stumbled, they rejoiced and gathered;\nattackers I did not know gathered against me,\ntearing at me without stopping.|Retain contrast with prior care and uncertain attackers term.
35:16|Like godless mockers at a feast,\nthey gnashed their teeth at me.|Choose feast reading of difficult phrase and preserve threat.
35:17|Lord, how long will you look on?\nRescue my life from their ravages,\nmy only life from these young lions.|Retain accusation of delay and irreplaceable life.
35:18|I will thank you in the great assembly;\namong a mighty people I will praise you.|Preserve public setting and future thanksgiving.
35:19|Do not let my treacherous enemies rejoice over me\nor those who hate me without cause wink at one another.|Keep collusive gesture and groundless hatred.
35:20|They do not speak peace;\nthey devise deceitful words against those living quietly in the land.|Preserve harm to peaceful residents.
35:21|They open their mouths wide against me,\nsaying, “Aha! Aha! Our own eyes saw it!”|Retain repeated taunt and claimed eyewitness evidence.
35:22|You have seen, LORD; do not stay silent.\nLord, do not remain far from me.|Set God’s sight against hostile witnesses and retain two divine forms.
35:23|Wake up! Rise to defend my cause,\nmy God and my Lord, to contend for me.|Preserve urgent waking imagery and legal case.
35:24|Vindicate me according to your righteousness, LORD my God;\ndo not let them rejoice over me.|Keep requested judgment grounded in divine righteousness.
35:25|Do not let them think, “Aha! Just what we wanted!”\nDo not let them say, “We have swallowed him!”|Clarify inward speech and retain consuming image.
35:26|Let all who rejoice at my harm be ashamed and humiliated;\nlet those who exalt themselves over me wear shame and disgrace.|Keep collective reversal and garment image.

35:27|Let those who desire my vindication shout for joy and be glad.\nLet them always say, “Great is the LORD,\nwho delights in his servant’s well-being!”|Retain supporters’ voice and divine delight in welfare.
35:28|My tongue will speak of your righteousness\nand praise you all day long.|Close with sustained speech and justice theme.

36:1|For the music leader. Of the LORD’s servant David.\nAn oracle of rebellion concerning the wicked lies within my heart:\nthere is no fear of God before his eyes.|Keep pinned my heart and the difficult oracle construction.
36:2|He flatters himself in his own eyes\ntoo much to recognize and hate his wrongdoing.|Choose self-flattery while documenting uncertain pronoun relations.
36:3|His mouth speaks harm and deceit;\nhe has stopped acting wisely and doing good.|Retain deterioration in conduct, not merely ignorance.
36:4|He plots harm on his bed,\nsets himself on a way that is not good,\nand does not reject evil.|Preserve planned wrongdoing and repeated moral refusal.
36:5|LORD, your faithful love reaches the heavens,\nyour faithfulness the clouds.|Keep parallel expansive images and distinct related terms.
36:6|Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains;\nyour judgments are a vast deep.\nYou save humans and animals, LORD.|Retain mountains of God idiom and nonhuman beneficiaries.
36:7|How precious is your faithful love, God!\nPeople take refuge in the shadow of your wings.|Keep value and protective wings.
36:8|They drink their fill of your house’s abundance;\nyou give them drink from your river of delights.|Preserve abundant drinking and river imagery.
36:9|With you is the spring of life;\nin your light we see light.|Keep repeated light and source of life image.
36:10|Extend your faithful love to those who know you,\nyour righteousness to the upright in heart.|Retain relational knowledge and ethical recipients.
36:11|Do not let the foot of pride come upon me\nor the hand of the wicked drive me away.|Preserve threatening foot and hand.
36:12|There the evildoers have fallen,\nthrown down, unable to rise.|Keep the sudden vision of completed defeat.
37:1|Of David.\nDo not burn with anger over evildoers\nor envy those who do wrong.|Render heat idiom and retain envy as a distinct danger.
37:2|They will soon wither like grass\nand fade like green plants.|Preserve fleeting vegetation imagery.
37:3|Trust the LORD and do good.\nLive in the land and feed on faithfulness.|Keep difficult grazing image and document alternatives.
37:4|Take delight in the LORD,\nand he will give you your heart’s desires.|Retain delight and promise without inserting conditions.
37:5|Entrust your way to the LORD;\ntrust him, and he will act.|Render rolling one’s way naturally while preserving agency.
37:6|He will bring your righteousness out like light,\nyour vindication like the midday sun.|Keep public vindication and increasing brightness.
37:7|Be still before the LORD and wait for him.\nDo not burn with anger over someone who prospers\nby carrying out evil schemes.|Connect prosperity to scheming without flattening waiting.
37:8|Let go of anger; leave fury behind.\nDo not burn with resentment—it only leads to harm.|Preserve the warning about anger’s consequence.
37:9|Evildoers will be cut off,\nbut those who wait for the LORD will inherit the land.|Keep land promise and repeated waiting.
37:10|A little while, and the wicked will be gone.\nLook closely at their place: they are no longer there.|Retain invitation to inspect their disappearance.
37:11|The humble will inherit the land\nand delight in abundant peace.|Preserve humble, inheritance, and well-being together.
37:12|The wicked plot against the righteous\nand gnash their teeth at them.|Keep hostile intention and bodily threat.
37:13|The Lord laughs at the wicked,\nfor he sees their day approaching.|Distinguish Adonai and preserve approaching reckoning.
37:14|The wicked draw their swords and bend their bows\nto bring down the afflicted and needy,\nto slaughter those who walk uprightly.|Keep vulnerable victims and actual lethal violence.
37:15|Their swords will enter their own hearts,\nand their bows will break.|Preserve reversal onto the attackers.
37:16|Better the little a righteous person has\nthan the wealth of many wicked people.|Retain quantity comparison without idealizing poverty.
37:17|The arms of the wicked will be broken,\nbut the LORD supports the righteous.|Keep power as arms and divine support.
37:18|The LORD knows the days of the blameless;\ntheir inheritance will last forever.|Retain attentive knowing and enduring inheritance.
37:19|They will not be put to shame in bad times;\nin days of famine they will have enough.|Preserve concrete famine and sufficiency claim.
37:20|But the wicked will perish.\nThe LORD’s enemies are like the splendor of pastures:\nthey vanish—vanish in smoke.|Choose pasture reading of ambiguous term and retain doubled vanishing.
37:21|The wicked borrow and do not repay;\nthe righteous give generously.|Keep economic conduct as the ethical contrast.
37:22|Those he blesses will inherit the land;\nthose he curses will be cut off.|Preserve blessing/curse parallel and implicit divine subject.
37:23|The LORD makes a person’s steps secure\nand delights in that person’s way.|Clarify agency in the second clause, noting another reading.
37:24|Though they stumble, they will not be hurled down,\nfor the LORD holds their hand.|Keep stumble distinct from final collapse.
37:25|I was young, and now I am old,\nyet I have not seen the righteous abandoned\nor their offspring searching for bread.|Retain personal testimony rather than changing it into a universal command.
37:26|They are always generous and lend freely;\ntheir offspring become a blessing.|Preserve ongoing generosity and generational outcome.
37:27|Turn from evil and do good,\nand dwell securely forever.|Keep imperative and promised enduring residence.

37:28|The LORD loves justice and will not forsake his faithful ones.\nThey are guarded forever,\nbut the offspring of the wicked will be cut off.|Retain the troubling generational contrast and pinned wording.
37:29|The righteous will inherit the land\nand live there forever.|Preserve the repeated land refrain.
37:30|The righteous speak wisdom;\ntheir tongues speak what is just.|Retain speech as ethical practice.
37:31|Their God’s instruction is in their hearts;\ntheir steps do not slip.|Link inward instruction and stable walking.
37:32|The wicked watch the righteous,\nlooking for a way to kill them.|Keep surveillance and murderous aim.
37:33|The LORD will not abandon them to the wicked\nor let them be condemned when brought to trial.|Retain courtroom setting and protective refusal.
37:34|Wait for the LORD and keep his way.\nHe will raise you up to inherit the land;\nyou will see the wicked cut off.|Keep patience, conduct, inheritance, and observed judgment.
37:35|I saw a wicked tyrant\nspreading like a flourishing tree in its native soil.|Preserve rooted power image and violent character.
37:36|Then he passed away—he was gone!\nI searched for him, but he could not be found.|Follow third-person passed and retain disappearance.
37:37|Watch the blameless; look at the upright.\nThere is a future for the person of peace.|Keep observation and open future or posterity sense.
37:38|But rebels will be destroyed together;\nthe future of the wicked will be cut off.|Retain contrast using the same future term.
37:39|The salvation of the righteous comes from the LORD,\ntheir stronghold in times of distress.|Keep salvation’s source and defensive image.
37:40|The LORD helps and rescues them;\nhe rescues them from the wicked and saves them,\nbecause they take refuge in him.|Preserve repeated rescue and closing refuge explanation.
38:1|A psalm of David. For remembrance.\nLORD, do not rebuke me in your rage\nor discipline me in your fury.|Retain uncertain liturgical title and parallel plea.
38:2|Your arrows have sunk into me;\nyour hand has come down upon me.|Keep God explicitly addressed as afflicting agent.
38:3|No part of my body is sound because of your indignation;\nthere is no peace in my bones because of my sin.|Preserve the speaker’s causal understanding and bodily distress.
38:4|My wrongdoings have risen over my head;\nlike a heavy load, they are too much for me.|Retain drowning and burden images together.
38:5|My wounds stink and fester\nbecause of my folly.|Keep disturbing physical detail and self-accusation.
38:6|I am bent and bowed very low;\nall day I walk about mourning.|Preserve posture and duration.
38:7|My loins are full of burning;\nno part of my body is sound.|Choose burning reading and retain repeated bodily complaint.
38:8|I am numb and utterly crushed;\nI roar from the turmoil of my heart.|Keep forceful sound and inner agitation.
38:9|Lord, all my longing lies before you;\nmy sighing is not hidden from you.|Retain Adonai and unseen grief made known.
38:10|My heart pounds; my strength has left me.\nEven the light of my eyes is gone.|Preserve loss of vitality and sight image.
38:11|My loved ones and friends stand back from my affliction;\nmy relatives keep their distance.|Keep relational abandonment without inferring contagion.
38:12|Those seeking my life set traps;\nthose seeking my harm speak of ruin\nand devise deceit all day.|Retain lethal plotting and sustained speech.
38:13|But I am like someone deaf, unable to hear,\nlike someone speechless, whose mouth does not open.|Keep the comparisons as the speaker’s inability to respond.
38:14|I am like a person who hears nothing\nand has no argument to offer.|Retain silence and absence of rebuttal.
38:15|For I wait for you, LORD;\nyou will answer, Lord my God.|Preserve waiting as reason for silence.
38:16|I said, “Do not let them rejoice over me,\nexalting themselves when my foot slips.”|Supply the implied negative request and keep stumbling image.
38:17|I am close to falling;\nmy pain is always before me.|Keep imminence and unrelieved suffering.
38:18|I confess my wrongdoing;\nmy sin fills me with anxiety.|Retain open confession and emotional burden.
38:19|My enemies are vigorous and strong;\nthose who hate me unjustly are many.|Follow pinned living/vigorous rather than replacing it with without cause.
38:20|Those who repay good with evil oppose me\nbecause I pursue what is good.|Follow the read pursuit form and preserve moral tension with confession.
38:21|Do not forsake me, LORD.\nMy God, do not stay far away.|Keep repeated appeal for presence.
38:22|Hurry to help me,\nLord, my salvation.|End with urgency and divine title.

39:1|For the music leader. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David.\nI said, “I will guard my ways so I do not sin with my tongue.\nI will muzzle my mouth while the wicked are before me.”|Retain personal name in title and deliberate restraint image.
39:2|I was silent, saying nothing, holding back even good words;\nbut my pain grew worse.|Keep the cost of silence and ambiguous good phrase.
39:3|My heart grew hot within me;\nas I brooded, fire burned.\nThen my tongue spoke:|Preserve the mounting heat before speech.
39:4|“LORD, let me know my end and the measure of my days.\nLet me understand how fleeting I am.|Keep mortality as the object of requested knowledge.

39:5|You have made my days a few handbreadths;\nmy lifetime is nothing before you.\nSurely every person, even standing firm, is only a breath. Selah.|Retain concrete measure and apparent stability overturned.
39:6|People walk about as mere shadows;\ntheir bustle is only a breath.\nThey heap things up without knowing who will gather them.|Keep shadow, breath, and uncertain inheritor.
39:7|And now, Lord, what do I wait for?\nMy hope is in you.|Retain the question and direct answer.
39:8|Rescue me from all my rebellions;\ndo not make me a fool’s laughingstock.|Keep personal guilt and social disgrace.
39:9|I am silent; I do not open my mouth,\nfor you are the one who has done this.|Preserve God’s agency and renewed silence.
39:10|Remove your blow from me;\nI am spent by the assault of your hand.|Retain the painful appeal against divine attack.

39:11|When you discipline someone with rebukes for wrongdoing,\nyou consume what they cherish like a moth.\nSurely every person is only a breath. Selah.|Keep moral discipline, moth, and repeated frailty refrain.

39:12|Hear my prayer, LORD; listen to my cry for help.\nDo not be silent at my tears.\nI am a resident alien with you, a temporary settler like all my ancestors.|Retain vulnerable residency before God and ancestral connection.
39:13|Look away from me, so I may brighten again\nbefore I go and am no more.”|Keep the unsettling request for divine withdrawal and unresolved ending.
40:1|For the music leader. Of David. A psalm.\nI waited and waited for the LORD;\nhe bent toward me and heard my cry.|Render emphatic waiting through repetition.
40:2|He brought me up from a roaring pit, from clinging mud.\nHe set my feet on a rock and made my steps secure.|Keep roaring and mud images with stable footing.
40:3|He put a new song in my mouth, a song of praise to our God.\nMany will see and fear and trust in the LORD.|Retain the linked responses and shift to our God.
40:4|Happy is the one who makes the LORD their trust,\nwho does not turn to the arrogant or those straying after lies.|Keep trust as allegiance and two rejected alternatives.

40:5|LORD my God, you have done so many wonders; your thoughts are for us.\nNo one compares with you.\nIf I tried to tell and recount them, they would be too many to number.|Retain both thoughts toward us and no comparison to you; separate clauses avoid making thoughts the sole object of comparison.
40:6|You did not desire sacrifice and offering;\nyou dug out ears for me.\nYou did not ask for burnt offering or sin offering.|Preserve pinned ears image rather than replacing it with body.
40:7|Then I said, “Here I am; I have come.\nIn the scroll it is written about me.|Keep the scroll’s relation to speaker open to a note.
40:8|I delight to do your will, my God;\nyour instruction is deep within me.”|Retain delight and embodied inward teaching.
40:9|I have announced righteousness in the great assembly.\nI have not held my lips back, LORD; you know.|Keep public proclamation and divine witness.

40:10|I have not hidden your righteousness in my heart.\nI have told of your faithfulness and salvation;\nI have not concealed your faithful love and truth from the great assembly.|Preserve repeated refusal to conceal and distinct covenant vocabulary.
40:11|You, LORD, will not hold your compassion back from me;\nyour faithful love and truth will always guard me.|Keep correspondence between unrestrained praise and compassion.

40:12|Troubles beyond counting surround me.\nMy wrongdoings have caught up with me, and I cannot see.\nThey are more than the hairs on my head; my heart has failed me.|Retain guilt, blindness, and overwhelming number.
40:13|Be pleased to rescue me, LORD;\nLORD, hurry to help me.|Keep doubled divine address and urgent appeal.
40:14|Let those seeking to destroy my life be ashamed and humiliated together.\nLet those who delight in my harm retreat in disgrace.|Preserve distinct lethal intent and pleasure in harm.
40:15|Let those who say to me, “Aha! Aha!”\nbe appalled at their own shame.|Keep taunt and reversal.
40:16|Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you.\nLet those who love your salvation always say, “Great is the LORD!”|Retain communal joy and recurring praise.
40:17|But I am afflicted and needy; may the Lord think of me.\nYou are my help and my rescuer.\nMy God, do not delay.|Keep vulnerability alongside past rescue, ending in urgency.
41:1|For the music leader. A psalm of David.\nHappy is the one who attends to the weak;\nthe LORD will rescue that person on a day of trouble.|Preserve thoughtful care and reciprocal protection.
41:2|The LORD will guard them and keep them alive;\nthey will be called happy in the land.\nDo not hand them over to their enemies’ desires.|Follow read blessed form and preserve shift into prayer.
41:3|The LORD will sustain them on their sickbed;\nyou will turn their whole bed in their illness.|Retain the difficult bed-turning image and person shift for a note.
41:4|I said, “LORD, be gracious to me;\nheal me, for I have sinned against you.”|Keep the speaker’s confession within the illness prayer.
41:5|My enemies say maliciously,\n“When will he die and his name disappear?”|Retain hostile desire for death and forgotten identity.
41:6|A visitor comes and speaks empty words,\ngathering harmful gossip in his heart;\nthen he goes outside and spreads it.|Clarify sickroom visitor’s duplicity without inventing an identity.
41:7|All who hate me whisper together against me;\nthey imagine the worst for me:|Keep collective whispering and open its content.
41:8|“A deadly thing has fastened on him;\nnow that he lies down, he will never rise again.”|Retain ambiguous destructive thing rather than naming a disease.
41:9|Even my close friend, whom I trusted,\nwho ate my bread, has raised his heel against me.|Preserve shared food and the betrayal image.
41:10|But you, LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up,\nso I can repay them.|Keep retributive purpose rather than softening it to recovery alone.
41:11|By this I know you delight in me:\nmy enemy does not shout in triumph over me.|Retain the speaker’s sign of favor.
41:12|You uphold me in my integrity\nand set me in your presence forever.|Keep integrity and enduring presence.
41:13|Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,\nfrom everlasting to everlasting.\nAmen and amen.|Retain the closing doxology and repeated amen.
42:1|For the music leader. A maskil of the sons of Korah.\nAs a deer longs for streams of water,\nso I long for you, God.|Bind title and thirsty creature image without modernizing it.
42:2|I thirst for God, for the living God.\nWhen may I come and appear before God’s face?|Follow pointed appear rather than silently changing to see.
42:3|My tears have been my food day and night,\nwhile people keep asking me, “Where is your God?”|Keep unceasing grief and hostile question.

42:4|I remember these things and pour out my life within me:\nhow I went with the crowd, leading them to God’s house,\nwith joyful cries and thanksgiving, a multitude keeping festival.|Choose procession reading and preserve remembered communal worship.

42:5|Why are you bowed down, my soul? Why do you roar within me?\nHope in God, for I will yet thank him\nfor the saving help of his presence.|Preserve pinned his face and distinguish this refrain from the later form.

42:6|My God, my soul is bowed down within me.\nSo I remember you from the land of the Jordan,\nfrom the heights of Hermon, from Mount Mizar.|Keep divine address here and all three geographical expressions.
42:7|Deep calls to deep at the roar of your waterfalls;\nall your breakers and waves have swept over me.|Retain overwhelming waters explicitly called God’s.
42:8|By day the LORD commands his faithful love;\nby night his song is with me, a prayer to the God of my life.|Follow read his song and preserve day/night movement.
42:9|I say to God, my rock, “Why have you forgotten me?\nWhy must I go about mourning under the enemy’s oppression?”|Keep trust title alongside accusation of abandonment.
42:10|Like a deadly blow to my bones, my foes taunt me,\nasking all day long, “Where is your God?”|Retain bodily force and repeated taunt.

42:11|Why are you bowed down, my soul? Why do you roar within me?\nHope in God, for I will yet thank him,\nmy saving help, my God.|Repeat the shared refrain exactly; render salvation of my face as my saving help, explaining the bodily image in a note.
43:1|Vindicate me, God; defend my cause against a faithless nation.\nRescue me from deceitful and unjust people.|Preserve legal appeal and collective hostility.
43:2|You are the God of my refuge. Why have you rejected me?\nWhy must I go about mourning under the enemy’s oppression?|Keep refuge and rejection together with the earlier question.
43:3|Send your light and your truth; let them lead me.\nLet them bring me to your holy mountain, to your dwelling places.|Retain personified guides and sanctuary destination.
43:4|Then I will come to God’s altar, to God, my overflowing joy.\nI will thank you with the lyre, God, my God.|Keep altar, music, and doubled personal address.

43:5|Why are you bowed down, my soul? Why do you roar within me?\nHope in God, for I will yet thank him,\nmy saving help, my God.|Repeat the shared refrain exactly; render salvation of my face as my saving help, explaining the bodily image in a note.

44:1|For the music leader. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil.\nGod, we have heard with our own ears;\nour ancestors told us what you did in their days, long ago.|Preserve title and transmitted communal memory.

44:2|With your hand you drove out nations and planted our ancestors.\nYou afflicted peoples and spread our ancestors abroad.|Clarify changing objects of the parallel verbs while retaining displacement.

44:3|They did not gain the land by their own sword;
their own arm did not save them.
It was your right hand, your arm, and the light of your face,
because you favored them.|Retain denial of human power and bodily divine images.
44:4|You are my king, God;\ncommand victories for Jacob.|Keep singular voice within communal prayer.
44:5|Through you we thrust back our foes;\nthrough your name we trample those who rise against us.|Preserve aggressive victory images.
44:6|I do not trust in my bow;\nmy sword cannot save me.|Keep first-person military disavowal.
44:7|You saved us from our foes\nand put those who hate us to shame.|Retain remembered collective rescue.
44:8|In God we boast all day long;\nwe will thank your name forever. Selah.|Keep shift to direct address and enduring praise.
44:9|Yet you have rejected and disgraced us;\nyou no longer march out with our armies.|Preserve abrupt contradiction of prior confidence.
44:10|You make us retreat before the foe;\nthose who hate us plunder us for themselves.|Keep God’s agency in defeat and enemy gain.
44:11|You hand us over like sheep for food\nand scatter us among the nations.|Retain slaughter and dispersion images.
44:12|You sell your people for nothing\nand gain no wealth from their price.|Preserve protest at a sale without benefit.
44:13|You make us a reproach to our neighbors,\na mockery and a jeer to those around us.|Keep God directly accused of public humiliation.
44:14|You make us a byword among the nations,\na people at whom others shake their heads.|Clarify gesture of derision and international setting.
44:15|My disgrace is before me all day;\nshame covers my face,|Preserve shift into singular lament and continue its cause.
44:16|at the voice of the one who taunts and reviles,\nat the sight of the enemy bent on revenge.|Retain both spoken and confronting hostility.
44:17|All this has come upon us, yet we have not forgotten you\nor been false to your covenant.|Keep the community’s claim of undeserved suffering.
44:18|Our hearts have not turned back;\nour steps have not strayed from your path,|Retain negation over both parallel clauses.
44:19|though you crushed us in a place of jackals\nand covered us with deepest darkness.|Preserve God’s agency and desolate animal habitat.
44:20|If we had forgotten our God’s name\nor spread our hands to a foreign god,|Keep hypothetical disloyal worship and its gesture.
44:21|would not God search this out?\nHe knows the secrets of the heart.|Retain rhetorical appeal to divine knowledge as support for innocence.
44:22|Yet because of you we are killed all day long,\ncounted as sheep for slaughter.|Keep suffering for God without harmonizing to later quotation.
44:23|Wake up! Why do you sleep, Lord?\nRise! Do not reject us forever.|Preserve provocative divine-sleep language.
44:24|Why do you hide your face\nand forget our affliction and oppression?|Retain unsoftened question about absence.
44:25|We have sunk down into the dust;\nour bellies cling to the ground.|Keep bodily prostration and abasement.
44:26|Rise to help us;\nredeem us for the sake of your faithful love.|End with relational appeal rather than invented resolution.

45:1|For the music leader. According to “Lilies.” Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. A song of love.\nMy heart overflows with a good word; I address my verses to the king.\nMy tongue is a skilled scribe’s pen.|Include each title element and preserve poet/scribe imagery.
45:2|You are the most handsome of men; grace pours from your lips.\nThat is why God has blessed you forever.|Retain explicit male beauty because the source names it.
45:3|Strap your sword to your thigh, mighty warrior,\nin your splendor and majesty.|Keep royal military dress and address.
45:4|In your majesty ride on to victory\nfor truth, humility, and righteousness;\nlet your right hand teach you awesome deeds.|Preserve difficult linked virtues and instructing hand.
45:5|Your arrows are sharp; peoples fall beneath you—\nthey strike the hearts of the king’s enemies.|Make the compressed arrow action clear without removing violence.
45:6|Your throne, O God, is forever and ever;\nthe scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of fairness.|Preserve consequential divine address and document alternative syntax.
45:7|You love righteousness and hate wickedness.\nSo God, your God, has anointed you\nwith the oil of joy above your companions.|Keep God/your God distinction and anointing comparison.
45:8|All your garments smell of myrrh, aloes, and cassia;\nfrom ivory palaces string music brings you joy.|Supply scent naturally and note uncertain musical term.
45:9|Kings’ daughters are among your honored women;\nat your right hand stands the queen in gold from Ophir.|Retain women’s distinct royal roles and prized gold.
45:10|Listen, daughter; look and bend your ear.\nForget your people and your father’s house.|Preserve the shift to the bride and the demanding instruction.
45:11|Let the king desire your beauty;\nhe is your lord, so bow before him.|Keep hierarchy and physical beauty without modernizing the marriage.
45:12|The daughter of Tyre comes with a gift;\nthe richest of the people seek your favor.|Retain city personification and gifts seeking goodwill.
45:13|The king’s daughter is all splendor within her chamber;\nher clothing is woven with gold.|Read inward location spatially rather than as moral inner beauty.
45:14|In embroidered garments she is led to the king;\nvirgin companions follow her and are brought to you.|Retain female attendants and return to male addressee.
45:15|They are led in with joy and gladness;\nthey enter the king’s palace.|Preserve plural procession and destination.
45:16|Your sons will take the place of your fathers;\nyou will appoint them princes throughout the land.|Keep masculine address and dynastic succession.
45:17|I will make your name remembered in every generation;\nso peoples will praise you forever and ever.|Retain poet’s promise to the king and international praise.
46:1|For the music leader. Of the sons of Korah. According to Alamoth. A song.\nGod is our refuge and strength,\na help readily found in distress.|Keep title and accessibility of help.
46:2|So we will not fear though the earth changes\nand mountains slip into the heart of the seas,|Preserve cosmic instability and continue the sentence.
46:3|though their waters roar and foam\nand mountains shake at their swelling. Selah.|Retain waters’ force and shaking terrain.
46:4|A river’s streams gladden God’s city,\nthe holy dwelling place of the Most High.|Keep singular river with multiple streams and sacred city.
46:5|God is within her; she will not fall.\nGod will help her when morning dawns.|Retain feminine city personification and dawn rescue.
46:6|Nations roar, kingdoms fall;\nhe raises his voice, and the earth melts.|Keep nation/water parallel and divine voice.
46:7|The LORD of Armies is with us;\nthe God of Jacob is our stronghold. Selah.|Establish the refrain exactly for repetition.
46:8|Come and see the LORD’s works,\nthe desolations he has brought upon the earth.|Retain destruction rather than replacing it with generic wonders.
46:9|He stops wars to the ends of the earth.\nHe breaks the bow, cuts the spear apart,\nand burns the wagons with fire.|Follow pinned wagons and keep military disarmament.
46:10|“Let go, and know that I am God.\nI will be exalted among the nations;\nI will be exalted throughout the earth.”|Render cease/release in the conflict context and mark divine speech.
46:11|The LORD of Armies is with us;\nthe God of Jacob is our stronghold. Selah.|Repeat the refrain without unnecessary synonym changes.
47:1|For the music leader. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.\nClap your hands, all peoples;\nshout to God with joyful cries!|Retain title and universal summons.
47:2|The LORD Most High is awe-inspiring,\na great king over all the earth.|Keep divine title and worldwide kingship.
47:3|He subdues peoples beneath us,\nnations beneath our feet.|Retain subjugation in the communal celebration.
47:4|He chooses our inheritance for us,\nthe pride of Jacob, whom he loves. Selah.|Keep inheritance and loved Jacob without assigning a narrower referent.
47:5|God goes up amid shouts,\nthe LORD amid the sound of the ram’s horn.|Retain ascent and instrument without inventing a ceremony’s details.
47:6|Sing praise to God, sing praise!\nSing praise to our king, sing praise!|Keep all four calls and their emphatic repetition.
47:7|God is king of all the earth;\nsing a song of understanding.|Render maskil’s wisdom association while noting uncertainty.
47:8|God reigns over the nations;\nGod sits on his holy throne.|Keep repeated God and royal imagery.

47:9|The nobles of the peoples gather
as the people of Abraham’s God.
The shields of the earth belong to God;
he is greatly exalted.|Keep difficult gathering relation and shields metaphor.
48:1|A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah.\nGreat is the LORD and greatly to be praised\nin our God’s city, his holy mountain.|Preserve title and location of praise.

48:2|Beautiful in height, the joy of all the earth,\nis Mount Zion, in the far north,\nthe city of the great king.|Retain north/Zaphon expression for explanatory note rather than correcting geography.
48:3|Within her citadels,\nGod has made himself known as a stronghold.|Keep city’s feminine reference and divine defense.
48:4|Look, the kings assembled;\ntogether they advanced.|Preserve alliance and movement toward the city.
48:5|They saw and were astonished;\nterrified, they fled in haste.|Keep rapid sequence of defeat without inventing battle details.
48:6|Trembling seized them there,\nanguish like a woman in labor.|Retain gender-specific birth comparison.
48:7|With an east wind\nyou shatter the ships of Tarshish.|Keep sudden direct address and maritime comparison.
48:8|As we heard, so we have seen\nin the city of the LORD of Armies, in our God’s city.\nGod will establish her forever. Selah.|Preserve received tradition confirmed by sight.
48:9|We ponder your faithful love, God,\nwithin your temple.|Keep communal reflection and location.
48:10|Like your name, God, your praise reaches the ends of the earth.\nYour right hand is full of righteousness.|Retain global reach and ethical hand image.
48:11|Let Mount Zion rejoice;\nlet the daughters of Judah be glad because of your judgments.|Keep daughters metaphor with towns as note possibility.
48:12|Walk around Zion; make a circuit.\nCount her towers.|Preserve invitation to inspect concrete defenses.
48:13|Take her rampart to heart; examine her citadels,\nso you can tell the next generation:|Keep observation serving intergenerational transmission.
48:14|“This is God, our God forever and ever.\nHe will guide us unto death.”|Retain difficult final death phrase and document other readings.
49:1|For the music leader. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.\nHear this, all peoples;\nlisten, everyone who lives in the world,|Preserve title and universal wisdom audience.
49:2|people of low and high standing,\nrich and needy together.|Render paired human designations socially and inclusively.
49:3|My mouth will speak wisdom;\nmy heart’s meditation will bring understanding.|Keep outward speech and inward thought.
49:4|I will bend my ear to a proverb;\nwith a lyre I will unfold my riddle.|Retain teacher also listening and musical explanation.
49:5|Why should I fear in evil days,\nwhen the wrongdoing of those at my heels surrounds me—|Keep threatening heels idiom and continue the referent.
49:6|those who trust in their resources\nand boast of their great wealth?|Identify the threatening wealthy without generalizing all wealth as guilt.
49:7|No one can ransom a brother\nor pay God the price for his life—|Keep specific brother and inability to redeem.
49:8|the ransom for a life is too costly;\none must give up the attempt forever—|Preserve parenthetic explanation and absolute inability.
49:9|so that he might live on forever\nand never see the pit.|Connect purpose to the impossible ransom.
49:10|Anyone can see that the wise die;\nfools and the senseless perish together\nand leave their wealth to others.|Retain shared mortality despite differences in wisdom.

49:11|Their inward thought is that their houses will last forever,\ntheir dwellings through every generation;\nthey name lands after themselves.|Follow pinned inward thought rather than silently changing to graves.
49:12|Human beings in splendor do not endure;\nthey are like animals that perish.|Keep the first refrain’s endure verb distinct from verse 20.
49:13|This is the way of those with foolish confidence,\nand of those after them who approve their words. Selah.|Preserve ambiguous followers’ approval and misplaced confidence.

49:14|Like sheep they are destined for Sheol; Death will shepherd them.\nThe upright will rule over them at morning.\nTheir form will waste away in Sheol, far from their dwelling.|Follow read form and retain difficult final relation in a note.
49:15|But God will ransom my life from Sheol’s hand,\nfor he will take me. Selah.|Keep personal hope without specifying timing or mechanism.
49:16|Do not fear when someone grows rich,\nwhen the splendor of their house increases.|Preserve warning against fear of wealth.
49:17|At death they take none of it;\ntheir splendor does not descend after them.|Keep descent and stripped possessions.
49:18|Though they congratulate themselves while alive—\nand people praise you when you do well for yourself—|Retain aside’s shift to second person.
49:19|they will go to the generation of their ancestors,\nwho will never see light again.|Preserve final darkness in the poem’s own voice.
49:20|Human beings in splendor, without understanding,\nare like animals that perish.|Keep changed refrain wording and wisdom emphasis.

50:1|A psalm of Asaph.\nThe Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks and summons the earth\nfrom the sun’s rising to its setting.|Preserve Asaph title and El, Elohim, YHWH in source order, followed by the summons spanning sunrise to sunset.
50:2|From Zion, the perfection of beauty,\nGod shines forth.|Keep explicit beauty and divine appearance.
50:3|Our God comes and will not stay silent.\nFire devours before him; a fierce storm rages around him.|Retain terrifying arrival and silence broken.
50:4|He summons heaven above and the earth\nto judge his people:|Keep cosmic witnesses and own people as defendants.
50:5|“Gather my faithful ones to me,\nthose who made my covenant by sacrifice.”|Preserve covenant-making ritual and divine summons.
50:6|The heavens declare his righteousness,\nfor God himself is judge. Selah.|Keep heavens as witness and judge’s identity.
50:7|“Hear, my people, and I will speak.\nIsrael, I will testify against you.\nI am God, your God.|Mark renewed divine speech and covenantal address.
50:8|I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices;\nyour burnt offerings are always before me.|Keep precise denial rather than dismissing all sacrifice.
50:9|I need no bull from your house\nor male goats from your pens,|Express refusal in context of divine ownership.
50:10|for every forest animal is mine,\nthe cattle on a thousand hills.|Keep comprehensive ownership and stated number.
50:11|I know every bird of the mountains;\nthe creatures of the fields are mine.|Retain knowledge and ownership of nonhuman life.
50:12|If I were hungry, I would not tell you,\nfor the world and all it holds belong to me.|Keep the hypothetical and ironic independence.
50:13|Do I eat the flesh of bulls\nor drink the blood of goats?|Preserve rhetorical challenge to feeding God.
50:14|Offer thanksgiving as your sacrifice to God;\nfulfill your vows to the Most High.|Keep thanksgiving’s possible sacrificial sense and vowed obligations.
50:15|Call on me on a day of distress.\nI will rescue you, and you will honor me.”|Close first speech with relational response.
50:16|But to the wicked God says,\n“What right have you to recite my statutes\nand take my covenant on your lips,|Keep new audience and challenge to empty recitation.
50:17|when you hate correction\nand throw my words behind you?|Retain active rejection image.

50:18|When you see a thief, you are pleased to join him;\nyou throw in your lot with adulterers.|Read ratzah as pleased approval and participation with a thief; retain separate company with adulterers.
50:19|You let your mouth loose for evil;\nyour tongue weaves deceit.|Keep unrestricted speech and crafting deceit.
50:20|You sit and speak against your brother,\nslandering your own mother’s son.|Retain intensified kinship betrayal.
50:21|You did these things, and I stayed silent.\nYou thought I was just like you.\nBut I will rebuke you and lay it all before your eyes.|Preserve mistaken inference from silence and confrontation.
50:22|Understand this, you who forget God,\nor I will tear you apart, with no one to rescue you.|Keep violent warning and absence of rescuer.
50:23|The one who offers thanksgiving honors me.\nTo the one who orders their way rightly\nI will show God’s salvation.”|Supply rightly from ethical context while noting compressed final clause.

51:1|For the music leader. A psalm of David, when the prophet Nathan came to him after he had gone in to Bathsheba.\nBe gracious to me, God, according to your faithful love;\nin your great compassion wipe away my rebellions.|Bind both title records and opening prayer, preserving the sexual euphemism with a note.
51:2|Wash me thoroughly from my wrongdoing;\ncleanse me from my sin.|Follow read imperative and retain washing/purification.
51:3|I know my rebellions;\nmy sin is always before me.|Keep acknowledged responsibility and constant awareness.

51:4|Against you, you alone, I have sinned\nand done what is evil in your sight,\nso you are right when you speak and clear when you judge.|Retain emphatic alone without using it to deny human victims.
51:5|I was brought forth in wrongdoing;\nin sin my mother conceived me.|Keep birth-to-conception imagery without assigning a specific maternal offense.
51:6|You desire truth in the inward parts;\nin the hidden place you teach me wisdom.|Retain obscure interior imagery with a concise note.
51:7|Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean;\nwash me, and I will be whiter than snow.|Keep ritual plant and cleansing comparison.
51:8|Let me hear joy and gladness;\nlet the bones you crushed rejoice.|Retain divine crushing and bodily restoration.
51:9|Hide your face from my sins;\nwipe away all my wrongdoings.|Preserve face turned from guilt rather than from the person.
51:10|Create a clean heart in me, God;\nrenew a steadfast spirit within me.|Keep creation and renewal as paired requests.
51:11|Do not throw me out of your presence\nor take your holy spirit from me.|Retain holy spirit language without adding a later doctrinal definition.
51:12|Restore to me the joy of your salvation;\nsustain me with a willing spirit.|Keep restoration of joy and willing disposition’s uncertain agency.
51:13|Then I will teach rebels your ways,\nand sinners will return to you.|Preserve future instruction arising from restoration.
51:14|Rescue me from bloodguilt, God, the God who saves me;\nmy tongue will sing of your righteousness.|Keep bloodshed responsibility and promised praise.
51:15|Lord, open my lips,\nand my mouth will announce your praise.|Retain God enabling the speech.
51:16|You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would give it;\nyou take no pleasure in a burnt offering.|Keep the speaker’s hypothetical offering and divine refusal.
51:17|The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit;\na broken and crushed heart, God, you will not despise.|Preserve plural sacrifices and repeated brokenness.
51:18|In your favor do good to Zion;\nrebuild Jerusalem’s walls.|Keep communal turn without resolving compositional history.

51:19|Then you will delight in righteous sacrifices,\nin burnt offerings and whole offerings;\nthen bulls will be offered on your altar.|Retain righteous sacrifices, burnt offerings and whole offerings without collapsing the paired terms; preserve final bulls and altar.

52:1|For the music leader. A maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, “David has come to Ahimelech’s house.”\nWhy boast of evil, you mighty man?\nGod’s faithful love lasts all day.|Retain historical title and abrupt contrast with divine loyalty.
52:2|Your tongue plots ruin,\nlike a sharpened razor, working deceit.|Keep tongue as destructive agent and sharp tool.
52:3|You love evil more than good,\nlies more than speaking rightly. Selah.|Preserve comparative loves and ethical speech.
52:4|You love every devouring word,\nyou deceitful tongue!|Keep consuming speech and direct address to tongue.
52:5|But God will tear you down forever;\nhe will seize you, pull you from your tent,\nand uproot you from the land of the living. Selah.|Retain escalating destructive actions and uprooting.
52:6|The righteous will see and fear;\nthey will laugh at him:|Keep both fear and laughter without softening.

52:7|“Here is the man who would not make God his stronghold.\nHe trusted in his great wealth\nand made himself strong through destruction.”|Preserve wrong refuge and difficult final source of strength.
52:8|But I am like a flourishing olive tree in God’s house;\nI trust in God’s faithful love forever and ever.|Keep living tree contrast to uprooted enemy.
52:9|I will thank you forever because you have acted.\nI will wait for your name, for it is good,\nin the presence of your faithful ones.|Retain unusual waiting for name and communal setting.

53:1|For the music leader. According to Mahalath. A maskil of David.\nThe fool says in his heart, “There is no God.”\nThey are corrupt and do abhorrent wrong; no one does good.|Keep title and this Psalm’s wrongdoing term distinct from Psalm 14.
53:2|God looks down from heaven on humanity\nto see whether anyone understands, whether anyone seeks God.|Retain God designation rather than harmonizing LORD from Psalm 14.
53:3|All have turned away; together they have become corrupt.\nNo one does good, not even one.|Keep comprehensive repeated indictment.
53:4|Do these evildoers know nothing,\ndevouring my people as they eat bread, never calling on God?|Retain unmarked my people voice and eating image.

53:5|There they trembled with terror where there was no cause for terror.\nGod scattered the bones of those camped against you;\nyou put them to shame, for God rejected them.|Preserve this Psalm’s distinct expanded judgment and second-person address.
53:6|If only Israel’s salvation would come from Zion!\nWhen God restores his people’s fortunes,\nlet Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad.|Keep communal longing and God rather than LORD.

54:1|For the music leader. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David, when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, “Is not David hiding among us?”\nGod, save me by your name;\nvindicate me by your power.|Bind both title records and preserve specific informants.
54:2|God, hear my prayer;\nlisten to the words of my mouth.|Keep doubled appeal to hearing.
54:3|Strangers have risen against me;\nruthless men seek my life.\nThey do not keep God before them. Selah.|Retain pinned strangers rather than substituting arrogant people.
54:4|Look, God is my helper;\nthe Lord is among those who sustain my life.|Keep the unusual among construction without excluding divine primacy.
54:5|He will turn evil back on those watching for my fall.\nIn your faithfulness, destroy them.|Follow read causative and preserve sharp turn into direct destructive appeal.
54:6|I will freely offer you a sacrifice;\nI will thank your name, LORD, for it is good.|Keep voluntary offering and good name.
54:7|He has rescued me from every distress;\nmy eyes have looked upon my enemies.|Do not add triumph or desire absent from the final clause.

55:1|For the music leader. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David.\nGod, listen to my prayer;\ndo not turn away from my plea.|Bind separate title with opening; keep plea against divine withdrawal.
55:2|Pay attention to me and answer.\nI am restless in my complaint, moaning|Let complaint run into the cause in verse 3; arid expresses restless distress.

55:3|at the enemy’s voice,
under the wicked man’s pressure.
They heap trouble on me
and pursue me in anger.|Keep hostile speech and pressure, plural turn and anger rather than adding physical blows.
55:4|My heart writhes inside me;\nthe terrors of death have fallen on me.|Retain embodied writhing and death terrors.
55:5|Fear and trembling come over me;\nhorror covers me.|Keep three cumulative fear expressions and covering image.
55:6|I said, “If only I had wings like a dove!\nI would fly away and settle somewhere.|Dove wish is escape and rest without adding heaven.
55:7|I would wander far away\nand spend the night in the wilderness. Selah.|Preserve wilderness lodging and pause within speech.
55:8|I would hurry to find shelter\nfrom the rushing wind and storm.”|Close escape wish at storm; refuge motif remains concrete.
55:9|Swallow them up, Lord; divide their tongues!\nI see violence and conflict in the city.|Keep destructive imperative and divided tongues rather than reducing to confusion alone.
55:10|Day and night they circle it on its walls;\ntrouble and misery are inside it.|Allow violence and conflict personified as circling without identifying invented guards.
55:11|Destruction is within it;\noppression and deceit never leave its square.|Retain civic public square and persistence.

55:12|If an enemy were insulting me, I could bear it.\nIf someone who hated me rose against me, I could hide from him.|Unfold the two negative counterfactual clauses naturally before betrayal disclosure.
55:13|But it is you—a man my equal,\nmy companion, my close friend.|Specific male friend and rank retained, no invented identity.
55:14|We shared the sweetness of private counsel\nand walked with the crowd in God’s house.|Keep intimate counsel contrasted with public shared worship.
55:15|Let death take them by surprise;\nlet them go down alive to Sheol!\nEvil lives in their homes and within them.|Follow read two-word death clause and retain living descent and imprecation.
55:16|As for me, I call to God,\nand the LORD will save me.|Contrast first person with enemies, distinct divine names.
55:17|Evening, morning, and noon, I complain and moan;\nhe hears my voice.|Preserve all three times and lament rather than substituting calm prayer.
55:18|He has ransomed me safely from the battle against me,\nthough there were many opposing me.|Render beshalom safety; with me can mean on my side or engaged against me, note choice.

55:19|God will hear and humble them—
the one enthroned from long ago. Selah.
They do not change,
and they do not fear God.|Keep ancient enthronement and difficult no-changes clause, note alternatives.
55:20|He reaches out against those at peace with him;\nhe has profaned his covenant.|Abrupt singular betrayer retained without adding name.

55:21|His mouth is smoother than butter,
but war is in his heart.
His words are softer than oil,
but they are drawn swords.|Preserve butter/oil and war/sword paired contrasts.
55:22|Throw your burden onto the LORD;\nhe will sustain you.\nHe will never let the righteous be shaken.|Keep casting and sustaining, indefinite burden rather than invented problem list.

55:23|But you, God, will bring them down to the pit of destruction.\nMen of bloodshed and deceit will not live out half their days.\nAs for me, I will trust you.|Keep half-days claim, bloodshed and final personal trust.

56:1|For the music leader. According to “The Silent Dove Far Away.” Of David. A miktam, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.\nBe gracious to me, God, for people trample me;\nall day an attacker presses me.|Title tune rendering tentative in note; preserve Philistines Gath and continuous oppression.
56:2|Those watching for my fall trample me all day;\nmany fight against me arrogantly.|Marom literally height, arrogance chosen over Most High address with note.
56:3|On the day I am afraid,\nI put my trust in you.|Fear and trust coexist, not denial of fear.
56:4|In God, whose word I praise—\nin God I trust; I will not be afraid.\nWhat can flesh do to me?|Retain repeated in God and flesh contrasted with human in verse 11.
56:5|All day they twist my words;\nall their thoughts about me aim at harm.|Keep words as object of painful distortion and evil intention.
56:6|They gather and hide,\nwatching my footsteps,\nhoping to take my life.|Follow read hide; bodily tracking and life threat explicit.
56:7|Will they escape despite their wrongdoing?\nGod, bring the peoples down in anger!|Difficult escape clause rendered rhetorical question; no added negative source text.
56:8|You have counted my wanderings.\nPut my tears in your skin-bottle—\nare they not in your record?|Preserve counting, tears and skin-container image rather than generic remembering.
56:9|Then my enemies will turn back on the day I call.\nThis I know: God is for me.|Keep day of calling and assurance not prediction of specific outcome date.
56:10|In God I praise the word;\nin the LORD I praise the word.|Repeat both parallel clauses and distinct divine designations.
56:11|In God I trust; I will not be afraid.\nWhat can a human do to me?|Preserve human noun different from flesh in earlier refrain.
56:12|God, my vows to you are binding on me;\nI will fulfill them with thank offerings.|Explain upon me as obligation without losing sacrificial thanksgiving.

56:13|You have rescued my life from death,\nand my feet from stumbling,\nso I may walk before God in the light of the living.|Render rhetorical have you not affirmatively; keep living light and walking purpose.

57:1|For the music leader. “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A miktam, when he fled from Saul into the cave.
Be gracious to me, God, be gracious to me!
I take refuge in you;
in the shadow of your wings I will take refuge
until destruction passes by.|Keep repeated plea/refuge and all title elements without selecting a cave location.
57:2|I call to God Most High,\nto God who brings things to completion for me.|Gomer completion left broad rather than inserting a detailed plan.

57:3|He will send from heaven and save me;\nhe will put my pursuer to shame. Selah.\nGod will send his faithful love and faithfulness.|Keep two sending clauses; reproach clause could describe enemy, note.

57:4|My life is among lions;
I lie down among those burning to devour—
human beings whose teeth are spears and arrows,
whose tongues are sharp swords.|Preserve intertwined fire/lion/weapon imagery and human referent, devour contextual expansion.
57:5|Rise high above the heavens, God;\nlet your glory be over all the earth.|Maintain exaltation petition and cosmic scope as refrain.

57:6|They set a net for my steps;
I was bowed down.
They dug a pit in front of me
and fell into it themselves. Selah.|Keep dejection and reversal without moralizing addition.
57:7|My heart is steady, God; my heart is steady.\nI will sing and make music.|Retain emphatic doubled heart and two musical verbs.
57:8|Wake up, my glory!\nWake up, harp and lyre!\nI will wake the dawn.|Keep glory self-address and audacious dawn-waking image, not simply early rising.
57:9|I will thank you among the peoples, Lord;\nI will make music to you among the nations.|Preserve international parallel praise.
57:10|Your faithful love reaches high to the heavens,\nyour faithfulness to the clouds.|Keep vertical paired qualities linked to verse 3.
57:11|Rise high above the heavens, God;\nlet your glory be over all the earth.|Repeat verse 5 exactly to support audible structure.

58:1|For the music leader. “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A miktam.\nDo you really speak justice, you silent ones?\nDo you judge people fairly?|Pinned elem silence difficult; preserve without silently repointing gods or rulers, note alternatives.
58:2|No! In your hearts you work injustice;\non earth your hands weigh out violence.|Judicial weighing image turned violent, heart and hands both retained.
